features.name: One named constant expiredReadDeadline = -1 * time.Nanosecond at BOTH stimulus sites, a mechanism-pin test, and the in-code LIMITATION
features.description: Design doc section 4, the only milestone: (4.1) one named constant with its comment block replacing BOTH `1 * time.Nanosecond` stimulus lines - read_deadline_test.go:254 inside TestDaemonReadDeadline/real-store-expired-deadline and :526 inside TestTimeoutStatusMirrorsSketch - with `d.readDeadline = expiredReadDeadline`; (4.2) a new ~26-line test TestExpiredReadDeadlineExpiresAtConstruction through PRODUCTION readCtx (it wraps, it does not replace), asserting the sign and that ctx.Err() is context.DeadlineExceeded at construction; (4.3) the LIMITATION(w-daemon-late-read-503) block appended to timedOut's doc comment in handlers.go - COMMENT ONLY, zero behavioural bytes. The mechanism: context.WithTimeout is WithDeadline(parent, now+d), and WithDeadline's `dur <= 0` branch cancels SYNCHRONOUSLY at construction (no timer, no goroutine) while any POSITIVE duration arms a time.AfterFunc that a fast :memory: read can beat - which is the measured ~1% base flake.

doc_defects_found.where: design doc section 6, MU-DEADLINE-DETACH inverse arm
doc_defects_found.summary: The stated inverse red SET is under-counted by one: TestDaemonReadDeadline/blocking-store ALSO reds, and the doc's next sentence says any red outside its set 'is unexplained and fails the arm'.
doc_defects_found.measured: go test -overlay ... -skip '^TestExpiredReadDeadlineExpiresAtConstruction$' -count=1 -v, run twice (base stimulus and head stimulus), identical both times: rc=1 with exactly 4 '--- FAIL:' lines - TestDaemonReadDeadline (parent), .../real-store-expired-deadline, .../blocking-store, TestTimeoutStatusMirrorsSketch; normal-deadline-answers-200 PASS.
doc_defects_found.mechanism: blocking-store sets d.readDeadline = 50 * time.Millisecond (read_deadline_test.go:271) and parks a getter until ctx.Done(). The mutant makes readCtx ignore the FIELD and use the 10 s package constant, so the park is never released inside test time and the subtest's own 2 s watchdog fires. Same phenotype as the other two reds - 'the field is ignored' - not an unexplained red.
doc_defects_found.consequence: An executor following the doc's sentence verbatim would score a CORRECT mutant as a FAILED arm.
doc_defects_found.resolution: Sprint plan section 4.2 T-MU2 carries the corrected, measured red set and requires ENUMERATION rather than an rc criterion. This is the ONLY place this plan overrides a literal doc sentence; it is overridden by measurement, not by argument, and the doc's underlying intent ('the red set is the assertion; an unexplained red fails the arm') is preserved exactly.

The planner's first mutation script targeted 'the occurrence after func TestTimeoutStatusMirrorsSketch', matched two, asserted count==1, and wrote NOTHING - after which the sweep read the UNMUTATED value 1 and would have scored as a clean arm without the assert.
doc_defects_found.lesson: A mutation that never landed prints the same green as one that worked. Hence the two-part landed-proof (sha256 movement AND a token grep at the intended site) and T-MU3's by-enclosing-function rule.

not_doing_ratified_do_not_fix: ARM B (a post-read expiry check answering 503 on a successful-but-expired read) and ARM C (both) - REJECTED ON THE RECORD in doc section 3 with measurements, not taste. Do not implement, do not 'improve toward'.
Weakening, moving or re-wording either test's assertions - the 503/Timeout pins are BYTE-UNCHANGED; only the stimulus moves.
Any retry or skip. The one operator re-measurement allowed in MU-STIM-POSITIVE's inverse arm binds the OPERATOR, not the committed gate.
Committing a -count loop to CI - AC3/AC4 are operator acceptance commands (doc section 7).

The 50 ms stimulus at read_deadline_test.go:271 (blocking-store) - deliberately outside AC5's pattern and safe at any positive value, because the parked getter cannot return until ctx.Done() fires (D4).
host/store/context_read_test.go - it already spells expiry correctly (D9).
A committed AST guard against future positive sub-deadline stimuli - doc section 10 declines it with its >=2-instance ledger.
Filing the successor rows: w-daemon-late-read-503 and the busy_timeout-vs-readDeadline ordering residual are CONTROLLER/RECORD actions, not sprint work.
Rows 20 (host/capsule) and 21 (host/archive) - untouched, and NO shared root cause is claimed.
tools/launchd/*, scripts/mission_decisions.sh, verify_*.sh, CI workflows, design_docs/sketches/worlddapi.ail, and the design doc itself.

The full mutation ledger for T-MU1/T-MU2/T-MU3: PRE hash, POST hash, the landed-proof grep, vet (and build) rc, the kill arm's counted --- FAIL: lines WITH the failure text, the inverse arm's ENUMERATED red set, and the restore hash == PRE.

execution.committer: THE CONTROLLER MAKES THE COMMIT - one commit for the one milestone. The executor never runs git commit/add/push/checkout/stash/restore or gh pr.
execution.worktree_rule: A SIBLING of the repo, never /tmp: /Users/voightkampff/dev/sunholo-data/.wt-iter94-timeout-flake
execution.restore_rule: Restores are `cp` from /tmp/w19_bak/ (taken OUTSIDE the repo). `git checkout --` is FORBIDDEN: the milestone is uncommitted by construction and git checkout -- would delete it.
execution.planner_wrote_zero_repo_bytes: All head/mutant probing used `go build/vet/test -overlay` with scratch files under /tmp/head94, /tmp/mu_stim, /tmp/mu_detach, /tmp/mu_revert. git status --porcelain empty and both sha256 unchanged afterwards.
